title: Spring Boot Auto-Configuration
summary: Auto-configuration scans the classpath at startup and registers sensible default beans based on what's present — add spring-boot-starter-data-jpa and it configures a DataSource and EntityManagerFactory for you, unless you've already defined your own.
mistakes: Saying 'Spring Boot has no configuration' — it has plenty, it's just applied conditionally (@ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean) instead of manually.
followUps: How would you exclude a specific auto-configuration class from being applied?
How does @ConditionalOnMissingBean let your own beans take priority over the defaults?
